validity.recommendation: no change to existence/classification; length/diameter confirmed as-is
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + CLASSIFICATION: real, correctly classified. This is FGT's certificated Jacksonville Expansion Project, FERC Docket CP15-144 -- application filed 2015-03-31 (Federal Register Notice of Application, 2015-04-17), FERC staff Environmental Assessment noticed 2016-01-15 (www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-05/CP15-144-000-Notice.pdf and the full CP15-144-000-EA.pdf, both verified live), certificate order 154 FERC P 61,256 issued 2016-03-30. Facilities per the EA: ~3.0 mi of 30-inch-diameter looping pipeline (Branford Loop, Suwannee/Columbia Counties, FL) + ~5.7 mi of 20-inch-diameter looping pipeline (Jacksonville Loop, Bradford/Clay Counties, FL) + a new compressor unit and re-wheel at Compressor Station 16 (Bradford County) + a new regulator station -- an interstate gas-transmission loop/compression expansion, correctly classified as a gas transmission phase, not a gathering/process line. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate -- one of the FGT roster's 17 distinct certificated phase rows (P4028-P4060 etc.), this one specifically CP15-144; no overlap with sibling phase facilities found. LENGTH: sheet LengthKnown=9.00 mi vs FERC's stated 8.7 mi (3.0+5.7) -- immaterial rounding difference, confirmed. DIAMETER: sheet '20, 30' in matches the FERC EA's 30-in Branford Loop + 20-in Jacksonville Loop exactly -- confirmed. Both Length and Diameter corroborated by only ONE independent primary source (the FERC EA/Notice, a regulatory finding distinct from the applicant's own website); I searched Florida PSC/DEP siting dockets and trade press (Pipeline & Gas Journal, NGI) for a second corroborating source and found none discussing this specific 2015-2016 project by name within the research budget -- tier held at medium pending a second source per the sweep's 2-source-owed rule, rather than forced to high on one document. Opened and read to exhaustion: CP15-144-000-Notice.pdf and CP15-144-000-EA.pdf (full text, ~2400 lines) -- see fills[] and the Capacity/Owner concerns below for other facts pulled from the same documents.

validity.recommendation: correct Capacity: FERC's own docket for this exact project states a TOTAL capacity of 75,000 MMBtu/d (60,000 MMBtu/d + a 15,000 MMBtu/d increment, both to Peoples Gas System delivery points in Florida) -- not the sheet's 50,000.00 MMBtu/d. Reconcile against GEM's own wiki entry for this same project too (see notes) before writing a final number.
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC (Capacity) -- material three-way disagreement, not silently passable. (1) SHEET: Capacity=50,000.00 MMBtu/d. (2) FERC Docket CP15-144 (both the 2016-01-15 EA and the 2015-04-17 Federal Register Notice of Application, verified live): 'The purpose is to provide a total of approximately 75,000 MMBtu/d of natural gas capacity' -- broken out in the EA body as 'firm delivery of 15,000 MMBtu/d to delivery points within the State of Florida. An additional 60,000 MMBtu/d would also be delivered to delivery points within [Florida]' -- both increments serve Peoples Gas System (PGS). (3) GEM'S OWN wiki page for this same project entry (read for leads only, never cited) states a THIRD figure: 'Capacity: 15 MMcf/d' (roughly 15,000 MMBtu/d -- apparently just the smaller of the two FERC increments, not the 75,000 MMBtu/d total), citing its own footnote [4] (eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php, a navigation page per this sweep's measured conditions, not a citable table). So the sheet's 50,000 figure is unsupported by either the primary regulatory record OR by GEM's own prior secondhand citation of it -- it does not correspond to the 75,000 total, the 60,000 or 15,000 sub-components, or the wiki's 15,000-equivalent figure. I could not identify any calculation that yields 50,000 from the underlying facts. This is a genuine sheet error, not a corroborated value: capping this cell rather than confirming it. Recommend the researcher who applies this batch resolve it against the 75,000 MMBtu/d FERC total (documenting whether GEM's convention is to record incremental-vs-total capacity, since the wiki's own 15,000 figure suggests the project may have historically been recorded as only the smaller increment).

validity.recommendation: correct Owner1: replace the self-referential 'Florida Gas Transmission Co LLC' 100% with 'Citrus Corp.' 100% (direct owner of the pipeline system), with Kinder Morgan Inc. and Energy Transfer LP each holding a 50% indirect interest in Citrus Corp. Same correction likely applies to every other FGT-cluster row on the sheet (see cross_row_leads) -- this is a systemic owners-tab defect, not P4030-specific.
validity.researcher_notes: ATTRIBUTION (Owner) -- the sheet's Owner1 = 'Florida Gas Transmission Co LLC' at 100% is self-referential: it names the OPERATING entity as its own owner, which is not how FGT's equity is actually held. Per Energy Transfer Partners' SEC 8-K exhibit (sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001012569/000095012311063823/h83324exv99w1.htm, verified live, names 'Citrus Corp.' and 'Florida Gas Transmission'): 'Citrus Corp., which owns 100% of the Florida Gas Transmission pipeline system' -- at the time of that 2011 filing Citrus Corp. was jointly owned by Southern Union Co. (later folded into Energy Transfer) and El Paso Corp. (acquired by Kinder Morgan in 2012). Present-day ownership (per independent public reporting, e.g. Wikipedia's Florida Gas Transmission article, corroborating the SEC filing) is Citrus Corp. 100% direct owner of the FGT system, itself held 50% Kinder Morgan Inc. / 50% Energy Transfer LP. I could not access ir.energytransfer.com's own press releases (403'd both attempts) as a third source, but the SEC exhibit is a primary corporate securities filing, independent of GEM and of FGT's own marketing pages. This misattribution is not isolated to P4030 -- every FGT-cluster row shares one Owner1 value on the operators/owners tab, so I expect the same defect on all 14 sibling FGT phase rows (named in cross_row_leads).

validity.recommendation: leave StartYear1=2017 and SegmentCost=47,000,000 USD as-is but flag both as independently unverified pending a better source
validity.researcher_notes: StartYear1 (2017) and SegmentCost ($47,000,000) both match what GEM's own wiki page states for this exact project entry (Start year: 2017; Cost: US$47 million), both citing the wiki's footnote [4] (eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php). That EIA URL is a navigation page per this sweep's measured conditions, not the underlying table, so I could not open the actual EIA source to check whether it independently supports these two figures or whether the wiki (and by extension the sheet) is simply repeating an unverifiable citation. I searched trade press (Pipeline & Gas Journal, NGI, S&P Global, Reuters) and FERC's own docket for an explicit in-service date or a stated project cost and found neither -- the EA's own 'Cost:' header field is blank, and no compliance/in-service filing for CP15-144 was locatable in the time available. 2017 is at least CONSISTENT with the certificate order's 2016-03-30 issuance plus a typical ~12-month construction window, so I am not flagging it as wrong -- but neither figure should be treated as independently confirmed. Recommend a follow-up pull of FERC eLibrary's CP15-144 docket for the post-construction in-service notification (which would state both the actual in-service date and, often, the as-built cost) before this is scored higher than medium.

fills.researcher_notes: Both sources are artifacts of the same FERC docket (the EA's own cover sheet, and the Federal Register's notice of that same application) rather than two fully independent origins, so held at medium tier despite two documents. Searched trade press for independent coverage of the March 2015 filing and found none.

No source located states an actual construction-start date. The FERC EA and Notice give facility scope and the environmental-review schedule but no construction commencement date; the certificate order's conditions (per the EA's referenced condition list) govern post-construction reporting, not a start date. Searched FERC eLibrary docket listing, Federal Register, and trade press (NGI, Pipeline & Gas Journal) for a groundbreaking/construction-start announcement and found none within budget. Leaving blank rather than inferring from the 2016-03-30 certificate order date.

The FERC EA defines MAOP in its glossary of abbreviations but never states an MAOP value for this project's facilities. No PHMSA/NPMS pull was completed for this specific segment within the research budget. Leaving blank rather than guessing a pressure rating from the 20/30-inch diameters.

Per gem_schema.md's documented gotcha, FuelSource names the upstream gas FIELD/FACILITY feeding the line, not the commodity type ('Natural Gas' would be wrong -- that's the Fuel column). The Jacksonville Expansion Project is a mainline loop + compression capacity addition on FGT's existing interstate system, not a new receipt-point tie-in to one named upstream field -- the FERC EA describes it purely in terms of delivery-point capacity (to Peoples Gas System), not a supply-side source. No single upstream field/facility could be attributed to this specific project scope; leaving blank rather than defaulting.
